claim: Two excluded emergency/service accounts authenticated in June 2026 using password plus SMS, despite the MFA exception having expired.
proves: The accounts authenticated using a weaker method than required by policy after their documented exception had expired.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that these accounts fall within the population covered by the A.5.15 control.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the expired exception was only a documentation lag, but rejected this because no renewed exception is on file.

claim: n.adamu was disabled 9 days after termination, compared with the 24-hour norm for 18 of 20 sampled accounts. vendor-backup has no HR record and remains active.
proves: The identity lifecycle process was not followed consistently for at least 2 of the 20 sampled terminations.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that vendor-backup access was misused.
alternative_considered: Considered whether vendor-backup was an exempted system account, but no such exemption is documented.

claim: The Q1 access review excluded privileged/service accounts from scope. The Q2 review had no sign-off by the audit date.
proves: The access review did not cover the full required population and was not completed by the required deadline.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that no informal review of privileged accounts took place outside the ticketed process.
alternative_considered: Considered whether an informal review of privileged accounts existed outside the ticketed process, but no supporting evidence was provided.

claim: HelpSphere was added on 14 May 2026 with access to patient-support attachments, but no completed security assessment or approved risk decision is on file.
proves: The required supplier security assessment was not completed for HelpSphere before or after onboarding.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that HelpSphere's security posture is inadequate. It only shows that the required security review is missing.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the privacy questionnaire could satisfy the requirement, but Procurement's own interview statement does not support this.

claim: The SoA evidence link mislabels the November 2025 incident exercise as the "2026 annual exercise."
proves: No exercise evidence from the current annual cycle was provided.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that no 2026 exercise took place, only that no evidence of one was provided.
alternative_considered: Considered whether a 2026 exercise took place but was only mislabeled in the file link, but the file metadata contradicts this.

claim: The only restore evidence on file is dated 22 Aug 2024 and relates to a retired database version. No restore test has been performed since the 2025 migration.
proves: No restore test has been demonstrated against the current production database version.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the restore would fail, only that no restore test has been performed.
alternative_considered: Considered whether successful daily backups were enough to demonstrate restore capability, but rejected this because backup success and restore capability are separate facts.

claim: The secure-development role training  was last completed in October 2024.
proves: The role-specific training has not been completed for more than a year as of the audit date.
does_not_prove: The source only states October 2024 and does not provide the exact date.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the LMS migration and loss of assignments explained the training gap. The evidence pack presents both facts but does not establish the cause, so the gap was retained rather than dismissed.

report_section: Test AT-08 / A.8.5 (prior finding NC-25-01 retest)
claim: The same excluded accounts from C-001 remain unresolved against last year's major MFA finding.
proves: The root cause of NC-25-01 remains unresolved, with privileged/sensitive accounts still lacking valid strong authentication.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that management's position that these emergency accounts are not privileged is wrong as a matter of policy interpretation. This remains a documented disagreement.
alternative_considered: Considered management's position that these are non-human accounts outside the required scope. This remains an open disagreement and was not resolved either way.

claim: Critical VULN-882 is 19 days old with no approved exception, against the 7-day SLA.
proves: A critical vulnerability exceeded the required SLA without a documented exception.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the vulnerability was exploited or that an exploitation attempt occurred.
alternative_considered: Considered whether an undocumented verbal exception existed, but no supporting evidence was provided and the SLA process requires an approved record.

claim: 4 of 48 production Linux hosts, including the primary billing worker, are silent. The monitoring ticket has been unassigned for 11 days.
proves: Production log coverage gaps remain, including on a high-value asset, with no active remediation owner assigned.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that a security event went undetected because of the coverage gap, only that monitoring coverage was incomplete.
alternative_considered: Considered whether 4 of 48 silent hosts could fall within an acceptable tolerance, but rejected this because the SOC Lead confirmed that no formal tolerance has been defined.

claim: CHG-2281 received retrospective approval after 8 business days. The policy requires approval within 5 business days.
proves: An emergency change exceeded the documented window for retrospective approval.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the change caused any adverse impact.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the 5-day policy applies differently to emergency changes, but no emergency-change exception was provided in the evidence pack.

claim: A real Severity-2 incident occurred on 6 June 2026. Legal was paged after 42 minutes, and one lessons-learned action has no owner.
proves: The incident process was used during a real event, but at least one resulting action has no assigned owner.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the incident response was mishandled. The 42-minute legal escalation was within the stated capability of the response roster.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the unowned action was immaterial because the incident was otherwise handled well. The finding was retained because an unowned action may not be completed.

claim: 15 of 412 active workers are overdue on general awareness training, including 4 developers and 2 privileged administrators.
proves: Some workers, including privileged users, have not completed the required security awareness training.
does_not_prove: Does not show how long each of the 15 workers has been overdue, only the total count and role breakdown.
alternative_considered: Considered whether 15 of 412 overdue workers was within normal operational lag, but retained the finding because the population includes privileged administrators.

claim: Six high-severity vulnerabilities exceed the 30-day SLA. Three also have expired accepted-risk records.
proves: Six high-severity vulnerabilities exceeded the required SLA, separate from the single critical vulnerability identified in C-009.
does_not_prove: The individual vulnerability IDs for these six findings were not provided in the evidence pack.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the expired accepted-risk records remained valid pending renewal, but rejected this because an expired risk acceptance does not automatically remain valid.

claim: CHG-2344 was a normal production release but was approved by its own implementer.
proves: The segregation-of-duties control was bypassed for at least one sampled change.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that this is a systemic pattern beyond the sampled change.
alternative_considered: Considered whether this was an isolated case. It was noted as such, but retained because it still represents a control breakdown in the sampled change.

claim: Identity audit logs are retained for 90 days, while the incident policy requires 180 days.
proves: Current log retention is below the organization's documented policy requirement.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the retention gap has affected any past investigation.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the 180-day retention requirement was outdated, but no updated policy value was provided, so the documented requirement was used.

claim: The Procurement Analyst stated in the interview that the privacy questionnaire was treated as the supplier security review for HelpSphere.
proves: The documented supplier security review process was replaced in practice with a different document.
does_not_prove: Does not prove that the privacy questionnaire was completely inadequate, only that it was used in place of the required supplier security review.
alternative_considered: Considered whether the questionnaire covered substantially the same risks as a security assessment, but this could not be verified from the evidence provided.
